text:
- chief complaint: right knee pain while running, worsening over time, for which the patient sought evaluation.
- history of present illness: the patient is a runner with intermittent right knee ache with activity, relieved by ice and rest and worse by end of day. Previously treated with ice and ibuprofen. Referred by primary care provider. No family history of arthritis or immune disease reported.
- physical examination: vitals within normal limits (BP 120/60, HR 58, RR 14), afebrile. Heart and lungs normal. Left knee normal. Right knee without redness or swelling, small effusion, pain on lateral side with palpation. Pedal pulses intact, no numbness or tingling. X-rays show well-maintained joint spaces, no fracture, no arthritis.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right knee ache with running, pain worse toward end of day after prolonged standing, lateral knee pain on palpation.
- new medications prescribed or changed: Tylenol 500 mg x2 and ibuprofen 200 mg x2, three times a day.
- follow-up instructions: no running for two weeks, begin physical therapy for the right knee, return to clinic in two weeks to assess progress; gym strength training such as squats only after first physical therapy appointment.
